headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can ingest files and generate outputs, but awesome-nlp is non-runnable and exposes no shared channel, so pairwise injection/leakage paths are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction channel is documented between awesome-nlp and ComfyUI. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while ComfyUI’s documented surfaces are files and API, not a bridge from the other agent. Without a shared channel, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste or file handoff is introduced between the two agents, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy untrusted text from awesome-nlp into ComfyUI prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared message queue.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and is non-runnable, while ComfyUI can read/write model files but is documented as offline and vendor-only egress. The pair lacks a shared workspace or authenticated data path, so leakage is not a default pathway; any leak would require unusual operator setup.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared filesystem with sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF ComfyUI is configured to send prompts or assets to an external service, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Store sensitive assets outside ComfyUI model folders.
Verify ComfyUI remains offline/vendor-only before use.
Remove any shared cloud sync from the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write, shell, or network capabilities, and ComfyUI explicitly lacks shell, filesystem write, git modification, and subprocess spawning. With no overlapping mutable write surface, there is no credible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI in its default non-writing mode.
Avoid mounting a shared writable repo into either agent.
Do not grant shell or git permissions to ComfyUI.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if shared writes are later enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is an awesome-list repository, not an active agent producing authoritative facts, and ComfyUI is a generator with no documented downstream action-taking authority. Since ComfyUI does not inherently consume awesome-nlp outputs as trusted inputs, cascading error is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator uses awesome-nlp content as a prompt source for ComfyUI without review, errors can cascade into generated outputs.
mitigations: Review any copied content before using it in prompts.
Treat awesome-nlp as reference material only.
Keep a human verification step before generation.
requires-engineering: add validation for imported prompt templates.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. awesome-nlp touches no data classes, and ComfyUI’s documented surfaces are local model files with offline operation; there is no evidence of a compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually introduced into ComfyUI workflows, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in prompts or assets.
Keep ComfyUI offline unless a compliance review is completed.
Document any retention settings for generated outputs.
requires-engineering: implement data-class tagging and retention controls.
